text.arabic_uthmani: ٱلَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا۟ مِن دِيَٰرِهِم بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ إِلَّآ أَن يَقُولُوا۟ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ۗ وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ لَّهُدِّمَتْ صَوَٰمِعُ وَبِيَعٌۭ وَصَلَوَٰتٌۭ وَمَسَٰجِدُ يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ كَثِيرًۭا ۗ وَلَيَنصُرَنَّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَنصُرُهُۥٓ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَقَوِىٌّ عَزِيزٌ

words.gloss_range: plural relative pronoun that carries the prior permitted group into a defining expulsion clause
words.prose: The opening relative pronoun makes the people from the prior permission visible as a class. It does not individualize them; it lets the next passive verb define them by shared expulsion and by the confession that follows.

topics.headline: plural relative class marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the referent is a shared class from the prior ayah, not one isolated example.
topics.reason: The fixed masculine plural relative pronoun apposes the prior group and introduces the defining clause.

topics.headline: bridge from prior passive group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the permission of 22:39 being carried directly into the expelled group of 22:40.
topics.reason: The boundary rows connect the unnamed recipients of permission with the relative clause that defines them here.

words.gloss_range: completed imposed expulsion, with the agents suppressed and the victims defined by endured removal
words.root_gloss_range: movement out from an interior or proper place; here Form IV passive narrows it to caused expulsion, while extraction and tribute associations remain secondary pressure
words.prose: {{ar:أُخْرِجُوا۟}} ({{tr:ukhrijū}}) defines the group by a completed injury they underwent. The Form IV passive makes removal imposed while leaving the expellers unnamed, and the root image of being drawn out from a proper setting sharpens the following loss of homes. It also places the verb in a Quranic expulsion-from-homes pattern (2:246; 3:195; 59:8), so the prior wrong of 22:39 becomes concrete displacement.

topics.headline: completed passive expulsion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices expulsion as the completed defining event of the group.
topics.reason: The perfect passive 3mp form defines the relative group by an endured event.

topics.headline: caused removal with hidden agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the form foregrounds coerced displacement rather than the identity of the expeller.
topics.reason: Form IV passive marks caused removal and suppresses the human agent.

topics.headline: extraction pressure without replacing expulsion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices removal as being pulled from belonging, while tribute or extraction branches remain background pressure rather than the local sense.
topics.reason: Root and derivative rows support extraction pressure, but local grammar selects passive expulsion from homes.

topics.headline: recurring Quranic displacement motif
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the word joining other expulsion-from-homes scenes such as 2:246, 3:195, and 59:8.
topics.reason: The supplied references put this passive expulsion in a repeated displacement field.

topics.headline: wrong specified as displacement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the prior abstract wrong becoming concrete removal from dwelling-place.
topics.reason: The boundary row ties 22:39 injustice to the specified expulsion in 22:40.

words.gloss_range: ablative source marker making the homes the point from which they are torn away
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) makes the expulsion spatially separative. The homes are not just a starting point; they are the origin from which the passive removal tears the group away.

topics.headline: separative source marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices expulsion as removal away from a concrete source.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the home noun and marks the source of expulsion.

topics.headline: separation rather than mere origin
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the preposition carrying rupture, not neutral travel-from language.
topics.reason: Its attachment to the expulsion verb makes separation the local force.

words.gloss_range: their own plural homes or domains, possessed and distributed across the expelled community
words.root_gloss_range: circling, dwelling, and domain fields; here plural possessed homes are selected, with return-center and territorial belonging as pressure
words.prose: {{ar:دِيَٰرِهِم}} ({{tr:diyārihim}}) makes the loss personal and collective: they are removed from their own dwelling network, not from abstract land. The root pressure of return and domain makes the homes feel like centers of belonging, while the local noun remains concrete plural homes. Its pairing with expulsion recalls other displacement scenes (2:246; 3:195; 59:8; 60:9).

topics.headline: possessed plural dwelling network
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices displacement from their own specific homes across the community.
topics.reason: The genitive plural with suffix binds the homes to the expelled group.

topics.headline: home as return-center and domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the home as an axis of return and belonging, while the local sense stays dwelling-place.
topics.reason: Root rows support circling, return, and domain pressure without replacing the concrete home noun.

topics.headline: distributed collective loss
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices multiple homes being affected, not one emblematic house.
topics.reason: Plural form plus group suffix distributes the loss.

topics.headline: expulsion-home pair across Quranic scenes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a recurring expulsion-from-homes pairing in references such as 2:246, 3:195, 59:8, and 60:9.
topics.reason: The supplied references connect this home term with expulsion contexts.

words.gloss_range: prepositional bāʾ attaching the no-right phrase as the manner or circumstance of expulsion
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) binds the legal defect to the act itself. The expulsion happens in a condition of no right, so the phrase does not sit outside the event as a loose comment.

topics.headline: manner phrase attached to expulsion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the absence of right traveling with the expulsion action.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the following construct phrase and attaches it to the expulsion verb.

topics.headline: accompaniment of legal defect
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the preposition making no-right a state accompanying the act.
topics.reason: The local phrase functions as manner or circumstance of removal.

words.gloss_range: construct noun of other-than-ness that negates right through an annexed phrase
words.root_gloss_range: otherness, alteration, and contrast; here the construct selects other-than-right as the local negating relation
words.prose: {{ar:غَيْرِ}} ({{tr:ghayri}}) negates through a noun in construct, not through a simple no-particle. It casts the expulsion as standing outside the domain of right, and the same surah’s without-knowledge formulas make the failure of right part of a broader pattern of deficient warrant.

topics.headline: construct negation by annexation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices negation built as a noun phrase, other-than right.
topics.reason: The word is a genitive construct head before the right noun.

topics.headline: otherness from right
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices injustice as a state of otherness from right, while broader change or jealousy branches are not local senses.
topics.reason: Root rows support otherness and change pressure, but local construct grammar selects other-than.

topics.headline: substantival negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a state of no-right rather than a bare verbal denial.
topics.reason: The noun form carries negation through construct syntax.

topics.headline: without-formula inside the surah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices 22:40 shifting a repeated without-formula from knowledge failures in 22:3 and 22:8 to right.
topics.reason: The echo row gives concrete same-surah parallels.

words.gloss_range: indefinite right under negation, denying any lawful, truthful, or reality-grounded warrant
words.root_gloss_range: truth, right, and established reality; here the indefinite noun under negation blocks any valid warrant
words.prose: {{ar:حَقٍّ}} ({{tr:ḥaqqin}}) is indefinite inside the no-right phrase, so the denial is total: no legitimate right is supplied. Its root field keeps legal right, truth, and established reality together, making the expulsion defective at more than one level. The phrase specifies the wrong named in 22:39 by turning cause for permission into a detailed legal defect.

topics.headline: indefinite under negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that no right whatsoever is left available.
topics.reason: Tanwīn under the negating construct universalizes the denial.

topics.headline: truth right and reality compressed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the expulsion lacking legal warrant, truthful basis, and reality-ground together.
topics.reason: The root field supports right, truth, and established reality as connected pressures.

topics.headline: tanwīn blocks a supplied exception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the form refusing a hidden specific entitlement.
topics.reason: The indefinite form prevents reading the phrase as only lacking one named right.

topics.headline: legal cause becomes legal defect
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the prior cause for permission becoming a detailed account of the wrong.
topics.reason: The boundary row relates the causal preposition in 22:39 to this legal defect in 22:40.

words.gloss_range: exception particle isolating the group’s confession as the only alleged ground
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَّآ}} ({{tr:illā}}) turns the accusation inside out. Whether read as connected or disconnected exception, the grammar leaves only the confession as the alleged ground and exposes the mismatch between that speech and the harm done.

topics.headline: exception exposes mismatch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the only stated charge is not a real offense.
topics.reason: The particle introduces the exception after the no-right phrase.

topics.headline: restriction to confession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the accusation narrowed down to a single utterance.
topics.reason: The restriction rows show the exception isolating the quoted confession.

topics.headline: creed becomes sole charge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices monotheistic confession being structurally cast as the alleged reason for expulsion.
topics.reason: The exception phrase interrupts the expulsion clause and identifies the sole ground.

words.gloss_range: subordinating particle nominalizing the act of saying as the content of the exception
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) makes the exception a content clause: the alleged offense is the fact of saying. The particle compresses the speech into a maṣdar-like charge before the direct utterance appears.

topics.headline: speech turned into content clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices saying itself becoming the alleged offense.
topics.reason: The particle governs the following subjunctive verb and forms a verbal noun-like clause.

topics.headline: finite verb stripped into charge-content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the grammar converting an action into the content of accusation.
topics.reason: The form binds the saying under the exception rather than presenting it independently.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive governed saying that introduces the quoted confession as the sole charge
words.root_gloss_range: saying and speech attribution; here simple declaration is selected, not debate or fabrication
words.prose: {{ar:يَقُولُوا۟}} ({{tr:yaqūlū}}) is governed by the content particle, so the saying belongs inside the exception rather than becoming a new report. The root field allows fabricated or disputational speech elsewhere, but here the form presents a plain communal declaration.

topics.headline: subjunctive governed declaration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the speech-act embedded as the charge.
topics.reason: The verb is subjunctive after the content particle.

topics.headline: plain saying not fabrication or debate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that a simple declaration, not proven falsehood or dispute, triggers expulsion.
topics.reason: Derivative rows name fabrication and dispute branches, but the local surface is simple saying.

topics.headline: governed mood marks embedded content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the confession grammatically subordinated to the exception.
topics.reason: The subjunctive mood keeps the verb under the particle.

topics.headline: direct speech defines identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the expelled represented by their own minimal utterance rather than an external label.
topics.reason: The direct speech rows connect this verb to the quoted two-word confession.

words.gloss_range: communal Lord-confession subject, asserting shared allegiance in a verbless sentence
words.root_gloss_range: lordship as mastery, ownership, nurture, and education; here communal lordship is selected
words.prose: {{ar:رَبُّنَا}} ({{tr:rabbunā}}) begins the quoted confession as a nominative subject: our Lord. The possessive suffix makes the confession communal, and the root field lets lordship include governing care and nurture rather than a bare title. As the first word of the two-word creed isolated by the exception, it makes communal lordship the only charge and the hinge into the later preservation argument.

topics.headline: subject of nominal confession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a stable verbless identity claim beginning with our Lord.
topics.reason: The noun is nominative as the subject of the quoted nominal sentence.

topics.headline: lordship with nurturing authority
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices God named as governing and sustaining Lord, while non-surface nurture derivatives remain supporting pressure.
topics.reason: Root rows support mastery, ownership, nurture, and education around the local title.

topics.headline: communal suffix binds the speakers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the expelled speaking as we, not as isolated individuals.
topics.reason: The first-person plural suffix makes the confession communal.

topics.headline: dense Lord-God confession formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the two-word creed functioning as the only charge.
topics.reason: The formula rows connect Lord plus God with confessional force.

topics.headline: hinge between expulsion and counterbalance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices communal lordship as the hinge between wrongful expulsion and the later preservation argument.
topics.reason: The structural rows place the word at the start of the isolated utterance.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name completing the confession and recurring through the ayah’s agency and seal
words.root_gloss_range: divine-name field of worship, awe, and possible bewildered love; here the proper name is selected as predicate and repeated anchor
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:allāhu}}) completes the confession as the predicate of our Lord. The proper name carries worship and awe pressure while remaining the local proper name. It then recurs through repelling, promised aid, and the final attribute seal, so the word that completes the expelled group’s speech also anchors the ayah’s answer and points to the same closing attribute formula in 22:74.

topics.headline: predicate completing identity sentence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the confession closing as a stable nominal assertion.
topics.reason: The divine name is nominative as predicate of the quoted subject.

topics.headline: divine name with worship and awe pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the proper name carrying devotional and overwhelming reference, while derivational disputes do not replace its local proper-name function.
topics.reason: The supplied dispute is valid background but local grammar selects the proper divine name.

topics.headline: divine name unifies confession and closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same name connecting confession, counterbalance, promise, and closing attributes.
topics.reason: The recurrence rows track the divine name through the ayah.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening the counterfactual argument after the confession
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) pivots from the local expulsion scene into a new argument. It introduces the counterfactual as a fresh stage, not as another item in the confession or expulsion details.

topics.headline: resumptive opening of new clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the discourse resetting into a counterfactual argument.
topics.reason: QAC marks the conjunction as introducing the counterfactual topic.

topics.headline: pivot from expulsion to principle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah scaling from a persecuted group to a general principle of preservation.
topics.reason: The structural row distinguishes resumptive use from mere coordination.

words.gloss_range: counterfactual prevention particle making existing divine repelling block demolition
words.prose: {{ar:لَوْلَا}} ({{tr:lawlā}}) is the hinge of prevention. Because divine repelling exists, the demolition that follows is presented as the result that would otherwise have happened, scaling one group’s injustice into a civilizational counterfactual.

topics.headline: counterfactual prevention construction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the clause arguing from an existing preventive condition.
topics.reason: The particle introduces a prevention-through-existing-condition construction.

topics.headline: nominal condition not finite event
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices repelling as a standing condition rather than a one-time verb.
topics.reason: The particle is followed by a nominal maṣdar subject.

topics.headline: hinge from injustice to civilization
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the argument widening from local expulsion to the preservation of worship-spaces.
topics.reason: The hinge row names the shift from Beat A to Beat B.

words.gloss_range: divine repelling as an operative counterbalance principle working through human subsets
words.root_gloss_range: pushing away, warding off, and handing over; here repelling is selected, with mediated delivery and mutual defense as qualified pressure
words.prose: {{ar:دَفْعُ}} ({{tr:dafʿu}}) carries the counterfactual clause: divine repelling is the principle that keeps demolition from occurring. As a verbal noun it can govern people like a verb, and the following some-by-some phrase shows the repelling working through human counterbalance rather than bypassing human agency. The same formula appears in 2:251, and within this surah it develops the divine-defense statement of 22:38 into an explained mechanism.

topics.headline: maṣdar subject as repelling principle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices repelling treated as an operative principle, not one episode.
topics.reason: The verbal noun functions as the subject after the counterfactual particle and governs an object.

topics.headline: repel with mediated-delivery pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices divine counterbalance as both warding off harm and directing force through agents, while handing-over senses remain secondary.
topics.reason: Root rows support repel, ward off, and deliver branches, but local grammar selects repelling.

topics.headline: compact Form I with defensive variant contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the surface as terse force, while the defensive qiraat widens the apparatus toward sustained defense.
topics.reason: The standard Form I maṣdar remains local while the variant supplies contrast.

topics.headline: formulaic counterbalance parallel with 2:251
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices 22:40 joining the same repelling-people formula found in 2:251.
topics.reason: The supplied rows give 2:251 as a close formula parallel.

topics.headline: chain from God through people to saved spaces
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices one word organizing divine agency, humanity, reciprocal means, and prevented demolition.
topics.reason: The structural rows identify this word as the pivot of the whole counterfactual beat.

words.gloss_range: genitive divine name specifying God as the agent of the repelling action noun
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine-name field; here bound in construct as subjective agent of repelling
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:allāhi}}) binds the repelling to God inside the construct phrase. The grammar makes the divine name inseparable from the action noun, so the counterbalance is not an impersonal social law.

topics.headline: genitive agent of repelling
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices God as the agent behind the counterbalance.
topics.reason: The divine name is genitive as the second term of the action-noun construct.

topics.headline: name fused to action noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices divine agency packed into one construct phrase rather than a separate clause.
topics.reason: The construct form binds the name to the verbal noun.

words.gloss_range: definite humanity as the collective object governed by divine repelling
words.root_gloss_range: human sociality and perception; here humanity is selected as the collective field being counterbalanced
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلنَّاسَ}} ({{tr:al-nāsa}}) is the object of the verbal noun, so the repelling acts upon humanity as a whole field. Root pressure from sociability and perception helps the phrase portray people as an internally dynamic social mass. Its object position carries the counterbalance formula of 2:251, while Surah 22’s opening crisis of humanity in 22:2 supplies a same-surah mass-humanity backdrop.

topics.headline: object of the action noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the maṣdar governing people like a verb.
topics.reason: The noun is accusative as object of the verbal noun.

topics.headline: human social field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices humanity as a social-perceptive collective, while root disputes do not change the local human noun.
topics.reason: The root dispute supplies pressure but local grammar selects the people.

topics.headline: definite collective humanity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the field as humanity, not only a named attacker group.
topics.reason: The definite article marks a recognized collective.

topics.headline: shared field in the 2:251 formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same human field active in the counterbalance formula of 2:251.
topics.reason: The intertext row connects this object to the repeated formula.

words.gloss_range: specified subset of humanity, appositive to the collective and internally linked by suffix
words.root_gloss_range: part, portion, and subset; here one portion of people is marked as the checked group
words.prose: {{ar:بَعْضَهُم}} ({{tr:baʿḍahum}}) partitions humanity from within. The attached suffix keeps the subset inside the human collective, and the paired some-by-some phrase models counterbalance through people checking people. The same some-by-some template in 2:251 makes this a recurring Quranic pattern of social restraint.

topics.headline: appositive internal partition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices humanity split into operative subsets.
topics.reason: The noun is accusative as apposition to the people.

topics.headline: suffix keeps subset internal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the checked group belonging within humanity itself.
topics.reason: The suffix refers back to the people.

topics.headline: reciprocal some-by-some mechanism
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the syntax itself modeling social counterforce.
topics.reason: The paired phrase shows one subset checked by another.

topics.headline: 2:251 counterbalance template
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same some-by-some formula recurring in 2:251.
topics.reason: The supplied echo ties the phrase to the earlier formula.

words.gloss_range: instrumental bāʾ marking one human subset as the means by which another is checked
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) makes the second subset instrumental. Divine repelling is therefore described as working by means of people, not merely upon people.

topics.headline: instrumental marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices intra-human agency as the means of repelling.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the second subset and marks instrumentality.

topics.headline: instrument fused to subset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the means attached directly to the repeated subset word.
topics.reason: The prefixed form binds instrumentality to the noun.

words.gloss_range: indefinite instrumental subset, open and distributable as the counterbalancing means
words.root_gloss_range: part or portion; here the second portion is the open instrument in the counterbalance phrase
words.prose: {{ar:بَعْضٍ}} ({{tr:baʿḍin}}) leaves the counterbalancing means open. The first subset is tied to the people, but the second is indefinite after the instrumental preposition, so the mechanism can distribute across different human agents. The repeated part-word makes the balance audible while case, suffix, and instrumentality keep the two roles distinct.

topics.headline: open instrumental subset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the instrument group left unspecified and reusable.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive after the instrumental preposition and indefinite.

topics.headline: case and suffix separate the two portions
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated root carrying two distinct roles.
topics.reason: The first portion is accusative with suffix; the second is genitive and indefinite.

topics.headline: audible reciprocal repetition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated part-word enacting the balance it names.
topics.reason: The echo rows preserve the repeated lexical shape of the phrase.

words.gloss_range: apodosis lām marking demolition as the certain prevented result of absent counterbalance
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) flags what would certainly have followed without the preventive condition. It welds emphatic consequence directly to the demolition verb.

topics.headline: answer marker for the counterfactual
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices demolition as the prevented result.
topics.reason: The particle introduces the answer to the counterfactual condition.

topics.headline: certainty prefixed to demolition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices consequence and demolition fused in one verbal opening.
topics.reason: The lām is prefixed directly to the passive verb.

words.gloss_range: intensive passive demolition of worship-spaces, agentless and physically architectural
words.root_gloss_range: pulling down buildings, with secondary worn-fabric disintegration pressure; here Form II passive selects thorough demolition
words.prose: {{ar:هُدِّمَتْ}} ({{tr:huddimat}}) names the catastrophe that divine repelling prevents. The passive suppresses demolishers just as the opening suppressed expellers, while the Form II and Quran-unique root make the imagined destruction thorough, physical, and architecturally concrete, with secondary fabric-like disintegration pressure.

topics.headline: passive verb governing the whole catalogue
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices one passive demolition extending over all four worship-space nouns.
topics.reason: The 3fs passive precedes and governs the nonhuman plural subject chain.

topics.headline: physical tearing-down with disintegration image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices concrete razing of devotional structures, while garment-wear imagery remains a secondary image of coming apart.
topics.reason: Root rows support architectural demolition and worn-garment pressure; local objects select buildings.

topics.headline: Form II intensive passive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the standard reading intensifying demolition beyond simple falling.
topics.reason: The standard Form II passive contrasts with a simpler Form I variant.

topics.headline: unique demolition root
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the threatened result carrying rare lexical weight in the Quran.
topics.reason: The supplied count rows mark the root as occurring only here.

topics.headline: rare intensive catastrophe
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices grammar, rarity, and Form II combining into a sweeping prevented catastrophe.
topics.reason: The synthesis row combines passive grammar, hapax rarity, and intensive form.

words.gloss_range: first protected worship-space class, shaped as monastic or tower-like structures in the passive subject chain
words.root_gloss_range: narrowness and pointedness; here it names hermitages or tower-like worship structures
words.prose: {{ar:صَوَٰمِعُ}} ({{tr:ṣawāmiʿu}}) opens the protected catalogue. Its first position anchors the passive subject chain, and the root image of narrow or pointed form lets the list begin with visibly shaped monastic or tower-like structures. The root occurs only here in the Quran, so the catalogue begins with rare architectural vocabulary.

topics.headline: first nominative subject of catalogue
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first noun anchoring the entire passive subject chain.
topics.reason: The noun is the first subject after the passive demolition verb.

topics.headline: vertical shaped worship structures
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the catalogue beginning with architecture whose shape is part of its identity.
topics.reason: Root rows connect the noun with pointed or narrow monastic structures.

topics.headline: indefinite diptote class noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a protected category, not one named building.
topics.reason: The indefinite diptote broken plural marks a class of structures.

topics.headline: opening of four-place sequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the list beginning with monastic or tower-like spaces before broadening.
topics.reason: The structural rows place the word first in the four-place catalogue.

topics.headline: corpus-unique architectural word
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices rare vocabulary at the catalogue’s opening.
topics.reason: The supplied count rows mark the root as occurring only here.

words.gloss_range: coordinating wa adding churches as the second equal subject in the worship-space catalogue
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds the second protected category under the same threatened demolition. The coordination keeps churches distinct while giving them equal syntactic exposure to the counterfactual.

topics.headline: second nominative coordinate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the list expanding without changing the governing verb.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the next noun into the passive subject chain.

topics.headline: distinct category preserved
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices churches added without dissolving the catalogue into a generic plural.
topics.reason: The structural row emphasizes distinction within coordination.

words.gloss_range: generic protected churches or chapels, with covenantal exchange pressure in the root field

words.prose: {{ar:يَنصُرَنَّ}} ({{tr:yanṣuranna}}) is the promised response: God will surely aid. The lām, imperfect, and heavy energetic ending secure it grammatically, while the Form I active makes God the direct giver of effective support, not one seeking help. The repeated root with the next verb creates a reciprocal frame echoed in 47:7, with support assurance also in 3:160 and 22:15, and its root field brushes against the protected Christian worship-spaces through the naṣārā association.

words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:allāhu}}) names the agent after an already marked third-person verb. The explicit subject reinforces that the promised aid comes from God, not from the grammar alone.

The same strength-authority doublet recurs in 11:66, 42:19, and 57:25, while here it expands the capability claim of 22:39 into a fuller power seal.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Those expelled from their homes without right for no stated cause except saying, Our Lord is God.
baseline_models.mechanism: Passive expulsion drives inhabitants outside a residential sphere. The exception leaves spoken allegiance as the only alleged offense, while without right denies a valid entitlement to remove them; confession and dispossession form one causal chain.

activation_trace.role: Emergence or separation from a settled state supplies the literal motion and makes forced exteriorization the mechanism.
The resident attached to a dwelling makes the lost homes an inhabited relation, not interchangeable property.
Otherness, negation, and exception sharpen the clause that leaves confession as the sole pretext.
A specific right owned by its bearer supplies the juridical relation that the expulsion lacks.
Speech as belief or doctrine makes the utterance a lived allegiance rather than an incidental sound.

changed_reading.before: The verse reports an unjust eviction caused by a religious statement.
changed_reading.after: The sentence stages persecution as the conversion of confession into an offense and as the severing of right-bearing residents from the sphere that housed their life.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Were it not for God's driving some people by means of others, monasteries, churches, prayer places, and mosques would be demolished.
baseline_models.mechanism: Counter-driving operates through one human part against another. Its success is measured by a negative event that does not occur, demolition, and by the continued presence of several unlike forms of worship rather than one victorious replacement.

activation_trace.role: Removing a thing and repelling harm supplies the counterforce that diverts destruction.
Parts or portions keep the human field internally plural and make reciprocal checking possible.
Casting down a building names the prevented endpoint by which the force is evaluated.
A Christian church contributes one explicit non-mosque institution to the protected plurality.
Places of worship widen the protected set beyond a single architectural or communal form.
A place of prostration completes the sequence as another embodied site of devotion.

changed_reading.before: God lets one group defeat another so religious buildings survive.
changed_reading.after: God's counterforce works through persistent human plurality, and its telos is non-demolition: unlike communities retain the material conditions for worship instead of one form erasing the rest.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The unlike buildings are linked by God's name being remembered in them abundantly.
baseline_models.mechanism: The locative phrase places repeated naming inside a differentiated series. Unity therefore lies in an enacted name circulating across sites, while the structures remain morphologically and communally unlike.

activation_trace.role: Remembrance running on the tongue supplies the repeated act that keeps each site alive as worship.
The name as public designation supplies the common sign borne across unlike institutions.
Growth in number or abundance makes naming a sustained social practice rather than a token occurrence.
The worshipped God is the shared referent that links declaration, preservation, remembrance, and support.

changed_reading.before: Several kinds of buildings happen to contain worshippers of God.
changed_reading.after: The ayah imagines a distributed name-bearing network: shared devotion connects differentiated sites without requiring architectural or communal sameness.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: God will surely support whoever supports Him; God is strong and mighty.
baseline_models.mechanism: The repeated support verb creates reciprocity but not equality of capacity. Humans aid and make manifest the cause attached to God's name; God aids and vindicates them, while gathered strength and prevailing inviolability ground the promise.

activation_trace.role: Aid and making manifest supply both sides of the repeated verb while allowing their capacities to remain asymmetric.
Vindication of the wronged gives support a justice-bearing sense alongside assistance.
Strength gathered like strands of a rope supplies reliable capacity behind the promise.
Might and inviolability after abasement make divine support more than temporary tactical success.

changed_reading.before: Those who help God's cause receive military help from God.
changed_reading.after: A reciprocal covenant links human manifestation and defense of the divine cause to divine aid and vindication, but the closing predicates keep ultimate efficacy on God's side.

context_deltas.mechanism: Distinct communities are named before separation is reserved for resurrection, and later judgment over disagreement is returned to God. Read back into 22:40, preserving unlike sanctuaries becomes worldly non-destruction without a claim that all doctrines are interchangeable.

activation_trace.role: Judgment that separates truth from falsehood places final differentiation with God at the named future time.
Divine judging between people reserves adjudication of their dispute rather than delegating erasure to a faction.
Parties taking divergent paths supplies the live disagreement that protection need not dissolve.
The explicitly differentiated church keeps the protected set confessionally non-uniform.
Plural worship places provide the material object of present protection while judgment remains deferred.

structural_cues: 22:17 lists several religious communities and locates separation on the Day of Resurrection.
22:40 lists several kinds of worship site inside a non-demolition counterfactual.
22:69 returns judgment over continuing disagreement to God.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies differentiated communities, deferred divine separation, protected differentiated buildings, and later divine judgment; I infer an arrow from deferred adjudication to present non-destruction. A live alternative is that the building list only magnifies collateral damage and does not formulate a coexistence norm.

changed_reading.before: The list merely says that warfare can damage many religions' buildings.
changed_reading.after: The list can enact a temporal ethic: disagreement and final differentiation remain real, yet no human party may settle them now by eliminating the others' places of worship.

context_deltas.mechanism: Good speech is paired with a guided path, while false speech is explicitly avoided. The focus confession is therefore not bare identity marking: persecution targets an utterance placed on a moral axis of guided versus fabricated speech.

activation_trace.role: Gentle direction toward truth links ethical speech to a traversable path.
Goodness opposed to corruption qualifies the kind of speech to which people are guided.
Utterance brought forth by speech supplies the explicit medium of the guided good.
False and bent speech supplies the rejected counterpart that sharpens the focus confession's ethical force.
The focus utterance as belief or doctrine anchors the contextual speech axis back in the eviction clause.

structural_cues: 22:24 repeats guidance around good speech and a praiseworthy path.
22:30 opposes false speech within a sequence about honoring sanctities.
22:40 makes saying a creed the sole stated pretext for expulsion.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a guided-good-speech sequence, a prohibition of false speech, and the focus creed; I infer that the creed belongs to this ethical speech field and that expulsion attempts to punish truthful allegiance. Alternatively, the exception in 22:40 may report only the persecutors' pretext without independently characterizing the utterance there.

changed_reading.before: The creed simply identifies why the victims were targeted.
changed_reading.after: The creed is also a morally situated act of speech: the persecutors sever people from home for walking the path of good rather than fabricated utterance.

context_deltas.mechanism: Obstruction is condemned where a sanctuary is made equal for resident and visitor; the House is prepared for moving and postural worshippers, and distant passes feed arrival. Preservation in 22:40 thus includes open approach, habitation, and use, not merely intact masonry.

activation_trace.role: Turning people away or obstructing them supplies a functional destruction that can occur before walls fall.
A spatial sanctuary marked by inviolability supplies the protected common destination.
Equality between two parties makes resident and outsider co-claimants to access.
A house as shelter joins dwelling and sanctuary while being prepared for recurrent users.
A wide pass between mountains extends sacred-space protection outward into routes of arrival.
Literal demolition remains the extreme endpoint within the wider disabling of access and use.

structural_cues: 22:25 equates resident and visitor at the sacred mosque and condemns obstruction.
22:26 organizes the House around circumambulation, standing, bowing, and prostration.
22:27 pictures people arriving through every distant pass.
22:40 moves from expelled residents to threatened worship buildings.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies equal access, an inhabited House organized for users, open approach routes, and threatened structures; I infer that blocking use and movement belongs to the same destructive mechanism as demolition. A live alternative is that 22:25-27 concern one sanctuary's special regime and only analogically extend to the plural sites in 22:40.

changed_reading.before: Defense protects religious monuments from physical destruction.
changed_reading.after: Defense protects sacred commons as functioning ecologies of access: residents, visitors, routes, rites, and buildings must remain connected.

context_deltas.mechanism: A rite is assigned to every community so that God's name is remembered, while divine oneness is asserted and later mutual contest over each community's rite is checked. This activates 22:40's several buildings as differentiated ritual forms joined by naming rather than homogenized practice.

activation_trace.role: A community or kind supplies the differentiated social bearer of each rite.
The place and performance of a rite bind communal practice to a material ritual setting.
Vocal remembrance supplies the shared act for which differentiated rites are given.
Divine oneness supplies unity of referent without erasing the preceding plurality of communities and rites.
Mutual pulling between parties images the contest that is told not to displace the call and guided path.
Remembering the name inside the focus buildings anchors the community-rite pattern to the protected list.

structural_cues: 22:34 places every community, its rite, remembrance of God's name, and divine oneness in one sequence.
22:67 repeats every community and rite, then checks contest and redirects to the Lord.
22:40 preserves several named building forms because God's name is remembered in them.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies communal differentiation, differentiated rites, shared naming, oneness, and a check on contest; I infer that protected plurality can be internally differentiated yet oriented to one divine referent. An alternative is that the rites are successive dispensations rather than a contemporaneous plurality, so coexistence remains a live but not exclusive reading.

changed_reading.before: The sites are a miscellaneous list united only by generic religiosity.
changed_reading.after: The sites can materialize a patterned plurality: communities retain distinct ritual forms, shared naming supplies relation, and oneness does not authorize ritual erasure.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding sacrificial sequence denies that flesh or blood reaches God and says that protective God-consciousness does. Consequently, supporting God cannot mean supplying a divine lack or treating material violence itself as the delivered good; it is loyal action ordered by God-conscious protection.

activation_trace.role: Attaining or reaching supplies the paired denial and affirmation that distinguish material output from accepted orientation.
Literal flesh supplies one material item explicitly denied as what reaches God.
Literal blood supplies the second material item denied as divine receipt.
Placing oneself within protection supplies the God-conscious orientation that reaches in place of flesh and blood.
Aid and manifestation anchor the correction to the focus phrase about supporting God.

structural_cues: 22:37 contrasts material sacrificial products with the inward-ethical orientation that reaches God.
22:38 shifts immediately to God's defense of believers.
22:40 calls for supporting God after defining the protected outcome as non-demolition and remembrance.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a denial of divine receipt of flesh and blood followed by defense and reciprocal support; I infer that support must be construed as enacted loyalty, not provision for divine need or sacralization of blood. The live alternative is that 22:37 regulates sacrifice only, making this transfer to 22:40 analogical rather than lexical.

changed_reading.before: Supporting God could be heard as materially supplying His cause, especially through combat.
changed_reading.after: Supporting God is protective and ethical participation that manifests the divine cause; neither divine need nor blood itself is the object delivered.

context_deltas.mechanism: The sequence moves from God's ongoing defense, to permission for those being fought because they were wronged, to their expulsion and the non-demolition rationale. Human counterforce is therefore a conditioned participation in defense after suffered aggression, not an unconditioned license to initiate domination.

activation_trace.role: God's repelling of harm supplies the governing defensive action before human permission appears.
Permission or authorization supplies a threshold and denies that force is self-authorizing.
Mutual fighting supplies the concrete violence already being directed at the permitted group.
Grievance and the demand for redress supply the moral injury that conditions permission.
Promised aid attaches to those already fought and wronged, locating support on the defensive side of the sequence.
Forced separation from home specifies the wrong that the focus ayah carries into its counterforce rationale.

structural_cues: 22:38 makes God the subject of defense before any human permission is stated.
22:39 uses passive fighting and passive wrongdoing for the permission's recipients.
22:40 adds passive expulsion and makes prevented demolition the counterforce's purpose.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies divine defense, explicit permission, already-suffered fighting and wrong, expulsion, and a preservation counterfactual; I infer a directional chain from injury to authorized counterforce to protected worship. A broader theory of war remains possible, but it cannot erase the local defensive conditions supplied by the sequence.

changed_reading.before: The verse generally authorizes believers to use force for religion.
changed_reading.after: The verse explains a bounded defensive intervention: authorization follows attack, injustice, and expulsion, and its stated measure is the prevention of erased worship.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah converts establishment in the land into prayer, distributive purification, recognition of the good, restraint of the reprehensible, and an outcome retained by God. Victory is not replacement domination but accountable institution-building.

activation_trace.role: Capability and establishment supply the post-defense condition whose use is immediately tested.
Purification and rectitude contribute a distributive obligation rather than private possession of victory.
The recognized good supplies a public norm that reason and moral knowledge can acknowledge.
Checking or restraining action supplies an internal limit on the community that has gained capacity.
The final outcome of a matter returns possession of history's end to God.
Reciprocal support is anchored to the civic obligations that immediately follow it.

structural_cues: 22:40 promises support after defining a plural non-demolition outcome.
22:41 begins conditionally with establishment in the land.
22:41 sequences worship, alms, public norms, restraint, and God's ownership of the outcome.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies promised support followed by a conditional portrait of established power and its practices; I infer that the latter is the operational test of the former. Alternatively, 22:41 may describe exemplary beneficiaries rather than formal conditions, but it still supplies the nearest picture of what supported power does.

changed_reading.before: Divine support culminates when the expelled gain control of territory.
changed_reading.after: Territorial capacity is only an intermediate condition; support is vindicated when power sustains worship, distribution, recognizable good, and restraint while leaving the outcome to God.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later ruin tableau joins a destroyed settlement, collapsed roofs, an abandoned well, and a raised palace, then asks travelers to reason with their hearts. The focus buildings therefore sit inside a civic ecology of inhabitants, water, shelter, status, and transmitted memory; preserving worship sites preserves more than monuments.

activation_trace.role: People gathered into a settlement supply the social whole within which buildings function.
Falling and collapse turn architectural ruin into the visible condition of an emptied settlement.
Raised roof or shelter supplies the structural layer on which the ruined settlement has fallen.
The well supplies communal water infrastructure rendered useless when users and settlement disappear.
A raised, strongly finished building contrasts material grandeur with failed communal continuity.
Reason that restrains ignorance turns encountered ruins into moral memory for later travelers.
Prevented building-collapse anchors the later civic ruin tableau back to the focus counterfactual.

structural_cues: 22:40 links expelled inhabitants to threatened worship structures.
22:45 juxtaposes settlement, roofs, well, and palace in one ruin tableau.
22:46 makes travel through such remains an occasion for heart-based understanding.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies habitation, worship buildings, settlement ruin, failed water infrastructure, contrasting monumental survival, and moral recollection; I infer that demolition names collapse of an interdependent civic ecology. A live alternative is that 22:45 is a separate warning tableau whose items are rhetorically accumulated rather than mechanically linked to 22:40.

changed_reading.before: The counterfactual concerns a set of religious buildings as isolated objects.
changed_reading.after: Their demolition would unravel inhabited civic memory: worship, dwelling, routes, water, shelter, and the capacity of later people to read a community's traces belong together.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later migrants may be killed or die and are nevertheless promised good provision. This weakens any reading in which support guarantees each expelled person a return, survival, or visible restoration; support can coexist with irreversible displacement and extend beyond immediate political outcome.

activation_trace.role: Moving from one home to another supplies a later form of displacement continuous with focus expulsion.
Literal killing blocks a simple equation between divine support and bodily survival.
Loss of life by death broadens the non-restoration possibility beyond combat.
Allotted gift or provision relocates the promise of care beyond immediate return to the lost home.
Separation from home anchors the migrants' later fate to the focus victims without requiring identity of every individual.

structural_cues: 22:40 promises support in the setting of expulsion and threatened demolition.
22:58 explicitly holds migration, killing or death, and promised provision together.
The packet does not narrate a universal return to the lost homes.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies expelled people, later migration, possible death, and continuing provision; I infer that support has a horizon wider than immediate restoration. The alternative is that 22:58 concerns a different migrant population, so it limits a universalized promise more securely than it identifies the focus group's fate.

changed_reading.before: God's promised support ensures that the expelled will survive, return, and reverse their loss in history.
changed_reading.after: The promise remains real without guaranteeing immediate restoration for every victim; divine care can accompany migration and death while the communal non-demolition norm remains operative.

context_deltas.mechanism: A later supported response is described by equivalence to what was suffered, renewed aggression, and a closing divine pardon. This constrains some-by-some counterforce as calibrated redress and interrupts the prospect of endless mirrored retaliation.

activation_trace.role: Likeness or equivalence supplies the proportional measure relating response to injury.
Transgressing the limit through aggression supplies the renewed wrong after the measured response.
Promised aid attaches to the party subjected to renewed aggression rather than to unrestricted retaliation.
Leaving punishment and effacing offense supplies an endpoint beyond reciprocal injury.
Human parts acting through and against other parts anchor proportional checking to the focus syntax.

structural_cues: 22:40 describes reciprocal human counterforce by repeating some.
22:60 marks a response as like what was suffered, then names a further aggression.
22:60 ends the support promise with divine pardon and covering.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies reciprocal parts, an equivalent response, renewed aggression, support, and pardon; I infer a constraint from equivalence and a directional exit from retaliation through pardon. A live alternative is that equivalence describes this case rather than legislating every instance, but it still disciplines the local counterforce reading.

changed_reading.before: Some-by-some describes open-ended reciprocal force as the engine of preservation.
changed_reading.after: Counterforce is a measured check triggered by aggression, bounded by equivalence, and oriented beyond retaliation toward the preservation and pardon that stop destructive recursion.

context_deltas.mechanism: God later holds the sky from falling on the earth, and the holding is framed by compassion toward people. This echoes the focus negative counterfactual: power is disclosed as maintaining a world by preventing collapse, not only by producing a victorious event.

activation_trace.role: Holding and restraining a thing supplies the preventive action that keeps collapse from occurring.
Falling and coming to rest supplies the blocked cosmic endpoint parallel to demolished buildings.
Tender compassion assigns care for people as the purpose of the restraint.
Merciful softness reinforces maintenance rather than spectacle as the governing telos.
Building collapse is the focus endpoint whose non-occurrence reveals effective counterforce.
Repelling harm connects preventive cosmic holding to protective human counterforce.

structural_cues: 22:40 uses a were-it-not counterfactual whose evidence is buildings not being demolished.
22:65 uses holding so that the sky does not fall except by permission.
22:65 closes the image with compassion and mercy toward people.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two prevented collapses and explicitly compassionate cosmic restraint; I infer that non-event and maintenance are a major grammar of divine power in the focus. The alternative is that the cosmic image asserts sovereignty without specifying a social model, so the transfer to institutions remains analogical.

changed_reading.before: Divine strength is visible chiefly when it overcomes an opponent.
changed_reading.after: Divine strength is also the compassionate capacity to hold a plural world in being; successful defense may be visible precisely as the demolition that never happens.

context_deltas.mechanism: The exact strong-mighty predicates recur after a rebuke for failing to appraise God, locating those capacities decisively with God. The surah then closes with strenuous effort, no imposed constriction, holding fast, divine patronage, and divine help. Human action remains real but cannot appropriate divine might as its own unrestricted sovereignty.

activation_trace.role: Gathered strength repeats the focus predicate while the rebuke marks God as its proper possessor.
Might and inviolability repeat the focus ending and resist transfer of divine status to a victorious group.
Exerting full capacity under difficulty keeps demanding human agency live without equating it with divine power.
Constriction or distress is explicitly negated, checking a reading of support as unlimited coercive burden.
A grasp that prevents and preserves makes holding fast a protective mode of agency.
Love, alliance, and supporting patronage place communal effort inside a prior divine relation.
The final helper title returns effective aid to God while retaining the community's striving and witness.

structural_cues: 22:40 closes reciprocal support with God alone described as strong and mighty.
22:74 repeats both predicates after saying that people failed to appraise God properly.
22:78 combines striving with no constriction, prayer, alms, holding fast, patronage, and help.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies exact predicate repetition under a rebuke and a closing network of effort, restraint, ritual, witness, holding, and divine patronage; I infer that human supporters may participate in power but may not possess God's unrestricted status. The alternative is that the repeated predicates are formulaic closure, though their placement still keeps ultimate efficacy divine.

changed_reading.before: God's strength validates the supported side's acquisition of superior power.
changed_reading.after: God's strength guarantees aid while also bounding the aided: their agency is strenuous, protective, ritual, distributive, and testimonial, never an appropriation of divine might.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it transfers saying from a human mouth to a building's signification. It remains anchored in the focus branch where a thing's saying can be its indication and in the buildings where the name is voiced; downstream prose should render it as a semiotic echo, not claim that masonry literally speaks or that this is the primary gloss.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus moves from people expelled for saying Our Lord is God to buildings in which God's name is repeatedly remembered.

activation_trace.role: A thing's saying as its indication permits the architecture to function as a public sign without literal speech.
Vocal remembrance inside the sites supplies the human speech that their continued presence houses and amplifies.
The name as designation makes each occupied building a bearer of public religious signification.
Demolition supplies the material operation by which this housed confession could be silenced.

changed_reading.before: Expulsion suppresses people, while demolition separately damages buildings.
changed_reading.after: The two acts can be read as one silencing operation across media: remove the confessing bodies and cast down the structures that let the divine name remain publicly audible.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because the d-w-r inventory's monastery image is an etymological or phonological fold near the ordinary dwelling sense, not the direct gloss of homes here. It remains worth carrying because expulsion from dwellings and threatened monasteries occur in one focus ayah; render it as a lexical resonance joining communal home and sanctuary, not as proof that the two nouns are identical.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Those driven from their dwellings are immediately followed by a counterfactual in which monasteries and other worship sites would fall.

activation_trace.role: The inventory's monastery or dayr folded near dar/dawr creates a latent bridge from lost home to threatened sanctuary.
The explicit Christian church keeps the resonance attached to an actual sanctuary in the focus list.
Plural places of prayer widen the communal-home image beyond the single monastery echo.

changed_reading.before: Homes belong to private displacement, and sanctuaries belong to public collateral protection.
changed_reading.after: A sanctuary can resonate as a community's inhabitable home, so forced removal and sacred demolition become two scales of the same unhousing.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This cross-domain model is surprising because it reads social counterforce through water-pressure and channel images from distant branches. It remains anchored in the focus roots d-f-a and n-s-r and is activated by the surah's rain-to-green-earth sequence; downstream prose should call it a material analogy for distribution and relief, never a lexical replacement for defense.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: God's driving of people through one another prevents sweeping demolition, and divine support sustains the protected result.

activation_trace.role: A flood or wave mass pressing against itself supplies a material image of potentially sweeping social force.
Water outlets and channels supply the image of redirecting pressure into bounded courses.
Rain as relief lets support be imagined as life-giving aid after destructive pressure is checked.
Channels arriving from afar into gathered water extend the distributed-infrastructure image.
Conveying water by pouring or irrigation activates the focus's latent channel branches in an actual renewal sequence.
Fresh green growth supplies the life-bearing outcome of distributed water rather than unchecked inundation.

changed_reading.before: Counterforce is only a collision in which one side blocks another.
changed_reading.after: As an exploratory material analogy, counterforce can redirect sweeping pressure like channels handling water, turning destructive concentration into distributed relief that keeps a plural social landscape alive.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the remote q-w-y branch of an empty, good-poor wasteland beneath the ordinary adjective strong. It remains anchored by the same focus root and by expulsion, threatened demolition, and the later emptied settlement; downstream prose should present an anti-emptying resonance, not redefine qawiyy or derive doctrine from wordplay.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The ayah closes with God as qawiyy after imagining residents expelled and worship buildings demolished.

activation_trace.role: An empty wasteland depleted of good supplies a remote counter-image latent under the final strength root.
Residents forced outside supply the first operation by which an inhabited place becomes empty.
Building collapse supplies the second operation by which communal good disappears from the landscape.
Emptiness and vacancy in the later settlement activate the final adjective's remote anti-landscape.
The abandoned well gives the emptied landscape a concrete loss of sustaining infrastructure.

changed_reading.before: Strong simply states God's superior force after the promise of victory.
changed_reading.after: At the level of contained resonance, divine strength answers a threatened process of emptying: it is power that keeps homes, sanctuaries, water, and communal good from becoming a vacant landscape.

strongest_changes: The some-by-some mechanism became conditioned defense: it follows attack, wrongdoing, and expulsion, is calibrated by equivalence, and is oriented toward pardon and non-demolition rather than open-ended domination.

The plural buildings became a protected regime of differentiated worship under deferred divine adjudication: disagreement remains real, but elimination of another community's ritual space is not its worldly settlement.
Sacred preservation expanded from intact masonry to accessible civic ecology, including residents, visitors, routes, rites, water, shelter, public norms, and moral memory.
Supporting God was revised away from supplying divine lack or sacralizing blood toward protective, ritual, distributive, and testimonial action whose efficacy remains God's.
The promise of support no longer guarantees immediate return or survival for every displaced person; migration and death can coexist with divine provision and a wider communal preservation horizon.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah sustained several coexisting readings without collapse: juridical confession and dispossession, pluralist non-demolition without doctrinal merger, bounded defensive force, accountable civic power, and divine maintenance as prevented catastrophe. The most unusual activations joined human speech to architecture as two media of confession, folded home toward monastery, modeled counterforce hydraulically, and heard qawiyy as a contained answer to social emptying.
remaining_uncertainties: The protected-building list may establish a norm of coexistence, magnify collateral devastation, or do both at once.
The every-community rite passages may describe contemporaneous differentiated rites or successive dispensations.
The proportionality and pardon sequence in 22:60 clearly disciplines this reading but may describe a case rather than state a universal procedure.
The speech-architecture, dar-dayr, hydraulic, and qawiyy-qawa activations are branch-backed analogies and should not be promoted into primary lexical glosses.
Divine support spans historical protection, moral vindication, and provision beyond displacement; the packet does not force one temporal horizon.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Defense preserves a plural ecology of remembrance.** `خ ر ج B002` supplies forced exit; `د و ر B001/B003` encircling homes and circulating affairs; `د ف ع B001` warding off; `ه د م B001` structural collapse; `ص ل و B007`, `س ج د B002`, and `ب ي ع B004` identify varied worship places. I infer that reciprocal restraint prevents power from erasing the built conditions of remembrance. Permission to resist reads as preservation of a multi-site worship ecology, not protection of one group alone.
2. **Divine strength is assembled support.** `ق و ي B001` images strength as rope-strands assembled; repeated `ن ص ر B001/B002` gives prevailing aid and redress; `ع ز ز B004/B001` reinforcement and might. Human support of God's cause and divine support are reciprocally phrased. I infer that defenders become strands within a stronger protective action. The conclusion reads divine might as the force that reinforces vulnerable human defense without confusing the two agents.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 22:65 later cosmicized the preservation mechanism: just as people restrain people from demolition, divine holding restrains the sky from destructive descent.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Counter-pressure preserves a plural ecology of worship.** Fixed `أُخْرِجُوا` activates `خ ر ج:B001` (passing out from within), and `دِيَار` permits `د و ر:B007` (one attached to a residence). The causal counterforce is `د ف ع:B001` (pushing away), distributed through portions of people (`ب ع ض:B001`) to prevent `ه د م:B001` (structural demolition). What is preserved is explicitly diverse: `ص م ع:B010` (the sawami/cowled-building image), `ب ي ع:B004` (Christian church), `ص ل و:B007` (places of worship), and `س ج د:B002` (prostration sites). `22:38-39` supplied defense and bounded permission; `22:41` supplies the conduct expected after enablement. The packet supplies social counterforce and multiple institutions; I infer that defense is justified by preserving worship-space as such, not by monopolizing it.
2. **A spoken confession is expelled from homes but re-housed in architecture.** The only stated cause of expulsion is fixed `يَقُولُوا` from `ق و ل:B001`, “our Lord is God”; later in the same ayah the divine name (`س م و:B005`) is mentioned abundantly inside protected buildings. The packet supplies utterance, displacement, and institutional remembrance; I infer that counter-pressure restores public habitat to the displaced speech. The line reads defense as protection of name-bearing practice.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later `22:41` turns preserved buildings into a program of worship, circulation, and norm-setting; `22:45` then shows impressive architecture emptied of social function. Both sharpen what institutional defense is for.

baseline.text: Onlar yalnızca Rabbimiz Allah'tır dedikleri için haksız yere yurtlarından çıkarıldılar. Allah insanların bir kısmını diğerleriyle engellemeseydi, içinde Allah'ın adının çok anıldığı manastırlar, kiliseler, havralar ve mescitler yıkılırdı. Allah kendisine yardım edene kesinlikle yardım eder. Allah güçlüdür, üstündür.

findings.text: İnsanların birbirini engelleyen karşı kuvveti yalnız bir topluluğu değil, farklı ibadet yerlerinden oluşan çoğul bir anma düzenini korur.
Evlerinden çıkarılanların Allah'ın adını söylemesi, sürülen sözün manastır, kilise, havra ve mescit yapılarında yeniden barınmasıyla karşılık bulur.

inter_ayah_rows.note: It bounds fighting to those who fight believers and prohibits transgression, giving a legal limit to protective counterforce.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It directly recalls prior expulsion, names persecution as graver than killing, and preserves the Sacred Mosque from initiating combat.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It frames fighting as ending persecution, a broad condition for unhindered devotion to God.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It explicitly joins barring God's way and the Sacred Mosque with expelling its people, judging that persecution more grave than killing.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Emigration and striving in God's way provide a broad continuation of the persecuted believers' response.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: God's help makes human defeat impossible, reinforcing the focus's assurance that divine aid is decisive.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The predicted testing and hurtful speech give a general setting for believers suffering because of faith.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It commands defense of oppressed men, women, and children who ask God for rescue, a protector, and a helper from an oppressive town.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It rebukes those remaining under oppression despite God's spacious earth, clarifying the urgency behind leaving a hostile place.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It promises abundance and refuge to one who emigrates in God's way, directly extending the focus's expulsion-and-migration setting.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It recalls a people who barred believers from the Sacred Mosque while forbidding retaliatory transgression.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It forbids hatred of a people who barred access to the Sacred Mosque from becoming injustice.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It recalls believers as few and oppressed in the land, fearing seizure, before God sheltered and strengthened them.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It names the plot to confine, kill, or expel the messenger and God's superior counter-plan.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It pairs emigration and striving with sheltering and helping, defining mutual protection among believers.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It warns that failure of believers' mutual protection produces persecution and great corruption in the land.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It again joins emigration, striving, shelter, and help as the marks of true believers.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It recalls opponents who planned the messenger's expulsion and commands resistance to their broken oaths.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It depicts God acting through believers' hands against hostile opponents and granting believers help over them.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It joins emigration, striving with wealth and persons, and higher rank with God.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It states that God helped the messenger at the moment of forced departure and strengthened him with unseen forces.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The messengers answer persecution with trust in God and resolve to endure the harm done to them.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Disbelievers threaten to expel the messengers from their land, followed by God's promise against the wrongdoers.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It promises a good settlement in this world to those who emigrated after being wronged.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It names those tested, then emigrating and striving, within God's forgiveness and mercy.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It limits response to harm by proportionality while commending patient endurance, refining the focus's counterforce.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It depicts an attempted driving of the messenger from the land, a direct parallel to forced removal.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The threat to stone the cave companions or force them back to another religion shows coercion directed at believers.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The proposal to establish a mosque over the cave companions supplies a limited building-and-remembrance parallel.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It promises provision to those who emigrated in God's way and were later killed or died.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It allows measured response to injury and promises God's help to one wronged again after responding.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It promises establishment, security after fear, and unhindered worship to believers who act rightly.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Noah's people threaten stoning, giving another direct form of violence against a messenger.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Lot is threatened with expulsion by his people, closely paralleling removal for a religiously marked stance.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: It exposes those who treat human persecution as though it were God's punishment, a limited contrast to steadfast faith.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Abraham declares his migration to his Lord, giving an early prophetic counterpart to leaving for God.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It directs believing servants to worship God where His earth is spacious, offering a practical horizon beyond hostile space.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It describes believers who defend themselves when oppression reaches them.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It permits a response proportionate to injury while elevating forgiveness and reconciliation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It removes blame from those who defend themselves after being wronged.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It assigns blame to those who wrong people and commit unjust aggression on earth.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Patience and forgiveness offer a secondary ethical limit beside the focus's preserving counterforce.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It directly promises that if believers help God, He will help and make them firm.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It recalls towns stronger than the city that expelled the messenger and were destroyed, directly linking expulsion and divine judgment.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It predicts that hostile fighters would turn away and find neither protector nor helper.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It distinguishes those who stand with God and His messenger from their opponents and calls them God's victorious party.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: It recounts the expulsion of a people from their homes, but without the focus's claim of wrongful religious persecution.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It portrays those who give emigrants shelter and aid, supplying the receiving community's counterpart to 59:8.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It preserves justice and kindness toward those who neither fight believers for religion nor expel them from homes.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It explicitly prohibits alliance with those who fight believers for religion, expel them from homes, or assist their expulsion.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It regulates the arrival of believing emigrant women, extending the communal consequences of migration for faith.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It commands believers to become helpers of God and recounts God's aid to the faithful against their enemies.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It says the believers were persecuted only because they believed in God, the Mighty and Praiseworthy.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It condemns those who persecute believing men and women and do not repent.
